title: Forty Microseconds: What a Fast Number Measures

scenes.tts: Could an enzyme step fit inside forty microseconds? First, you need to know what that number measures.
scenes.caption: Could an enzyme step fit inside 40 microseconds? First, you need to know what that number measures.
scenes.visual: Title card: Forty Microseconds: What a Fast Number Measures. A stopwatch reading 40 μs. Question on screen: could an enzyme fit in here?
scenes.narration: Could an enzyme step fit inside 40 microseconds? First, you need to know what that number measures.

scenes.tts: In nineteen seventy nine, Corey and Hudspeth moved the hair bundles of a bullfrog sacculus, in a dish.
scenes.caption: In 1979, Corey and Hudspeth moved the hair bundles of a bullfrog sacculus, in a dish.
scenes.visual: A flat sheet of hair cells from a bullfrog sacculus in a dish; a glass probe touches the bundles. Label: Corey and Hudspeth, 1979.
scenes.narration: In 1979, Corey and Hudspeth moved the hair bundles of a bullfrog sacculus, in a dish.

scenes.tts: They recorded the transepithelial microphonic. That is the summed electrical response across the whole sheet of cells.
scenes.visual: One electrode above the sheet and one below, wired to a box labelled summed response of the sheet.
scenes.narration: They recorded the transepithelial microphonic. That is the summed electrical response across the whole sheet of cells.

scenes.tts: The epithelium's own electrical time constant slows that signal. So the recorded delay is longer than the true one.
scenes.visual: A raw trace rises late and smoothly; a corrected trace beside it rises earlier. Label: correct for the epithelium's time constant.
scenes.narration: The epithelium's own electrical time constant slows that signal. So the recorded delay is longer than the true one.

scenes.tts: After correcting for it, the delay was forty microseconds, at twenty two degrees Celsius.
scenes.caption: After correcting for it, the delay was 40 microseconds, at 22 degrees Celsius.
scenes.visual: Number on screen: corrected delay 40 μs, 22 degrees C, bullfrog sacculus.
scenes.narration: After correcting for it, the delay was 40 microseconds, at 22 degrees Celsius.

scenes.tts: Predict. Suppose an enzyme had to make a chemical messenger between the bundle and the channel. Could the response begin that fast?
scenes.visual: A bundle, a small enzyme, a messenger molecule and a channel in a row, beside a 40 μs clock. Text: enzyme step inside 40 μs?
scenes.narration: Predict. Suppose an enzyme had to make a chemical messenger between the bundle and the channel. Could the response begin that fast?

scenes.tts: Only with great difficulty. Over a gap of nanometres, free diffusion can be fast. But that alone does not say how soon the messenger finds and binds a channel.
scenes.visual: A probability cloud spreads from a messenger's source across a short gap to a channel. Label: illustrative free diffusion, D = 300 μm²/s; root-mean-square spread about 270 nm in 40 μs.
scenes.narration: Only with great difficulty. Over a gap of nanometres, free diffusion can be fast. But that alone does not say how soon the messenger finds and binds a channel.

scenes.tts: Making it is tight too. In a simple constant-rate model, one enzyme at four thousand turnovers a second makes, on average, only point one six molecule. That is about a fifteen percent chance of making even one.
scenes.caption: Making it is tight too. In a simple constant-rate model, one enzyme at 4,000 turnovers a second makes, on average, only 0.16 molecule. That is about a 15 percent chance of making even one.
scenes.visual: An enzyme counter runs against the 40 μs clock. The clock stops. Label: constant-rate Poisson model; 0.16 expected products per active enzyme at 4,000 per second; chance of at least one about 15%.
scenes.narration: Making it is tight too. In a simple constant-rate model, one enzyme at 4,000 turnovers a second makes, on average, only 0.16 molecule. That is about a 15 percent chance of making even one.

scenes.tts: Many enzymes could make more. To test a messenger mechanism, we would need its enzyme numbers, activation and binding rates, geometry, and the messenger level that changes the current. This is a model check, not a result of the nineteen seventy nine experiment.
scenes.caption: Many enzymes could make more. To test a messenger mechanism, we would need its enzyme numbers, activation and binding rates, geometry, and the messenger level that changes the current. This is a model check, not a result of the 1979 experiment.
scenes.visual: Several enzymes light up around one channel, tagged hypothetical arrangement. Small tag on screen: a model check, not a result of the 1979 experiment.
scenes.narration: Many enzymes could make more. To test a messenger mechanism, we would need its enzyme numbers, activation and binding rates, geometry, and the messenger level that changes the current. This is a model check, not a result of the 1979 experiment.

scenes.tts: Now, what the number is not. It is not the opening time of one channel. And it is not a mouse number.
scenes.visual: The sheet of cells with one dashed channel marked with a question mark. Two crossed-out labels: one channel's opening time; a mouse number.
scenes.narration: Now, what the number is not. It is not the opening time of one channel. And it is not a mouse number.

scenes.tts: Channel speed was measured directly later. Ricci and colleagues found time constants as short as about fifty microseconds, in turtle hair cells.
scenes.caption: Channel speed was measured directly later. Ricci and colleagues found time constants as short as about 50 microseconds, in turtle hair cells.
scenes.visual: A patch pipette on a turtle hair cell; a current trace rising fast. Label: Ricci and colleagues, 2005; time constant as short as about 50 μs.
scenes.narration: Channel speed was measured directly later. Ricci and colleagues found time constants as short as about 50 microseconds, in turtle hair cells.

scenes.tts: So in turtle hair cells, channels do open on this time scale. The nineteen seventy nine number simply measured something else.
scenes.caption: So in turtle hair cells, channels do open on this time scale. The 1979 number simply measured something else.
scenes.visual: The tissue trace and the channel trace side by side, labelled tissue latency and channel time constant.
scenes.narration: So in turtle hair cells, channels do open on this time scale. The 1979 number simply measured something else.

scenes.tts: Four kinds of number are often merged. A tissue response latency is the delay of a whole population of cells.
scenes.visual: Four blank cards in a row. Card 1 turns: tissue response latency, with a sheet-of-cells icon. Example: 40 μs, bullfrog sacculus.
scenes.narration: Four kinds of number are often merged. A tissue response latency is the delay of a whole population of cells.

scenes.tts: A channel activation time constant is how fast current rises in a patch or cell.
scenes.visual: Card 2 turns: channel activation time constant, with a patch-pipette icon. Example: about 50 μs, turtle hair cells.
scenes.narration: A channel activation time constant is how fast current rises in a patch or cell.

scenes.tts: A molecular gain counts output events per input event.
scenes.visual: Card 3 turns: molecular gain, with a ladder icon. Example: about 12 to 14 effective complexes per activated rhodopsin.
scenes.narration: A molecular gain counts output events per input event.

scenes.tts: And a behavioural latency runs from stimulus to movement, through conduction, spinal circuits and muscle.
scenes.visual: Card 4 turns: behavioural latency, with a running-mouse icon. Text: no channel time constant stands in for it.
scenes.narration: And a behavioural latency runs from stimulus to movement, through conduction, spinal circuits and muscle.

scenes.tts: Speed can be compatible with a candidate channel. But speed alone does not identify it.
scenes.visual: A candidate channel with a tick for speed, and a sign: speed alone is not proof.
scenes.narration: Speed can be compatible with a candidate channel. But speed alone does not identify it.

scenes.tts: So before you compare two speeds, ask whether they are the same kind of number.
scenes.visual: Takeaway card: Before you compare two speeds, ask whether they are the same kind of number.
scenes.narration: So before you compare two speeds, ask whether they are the same kind of number.
